title: cat /proc/version
subtitle: The kernel names itself — one line, not a man page
what_you_see:
$ cat /proc/version
IR0 version 0.0.1-rc5 … (built DATE TIME by user@host with gcc)
why_it_matters: This is how the running system identifies itself. The string comes from IR0_VERSION_STRING and the build stamp — the same source uname(2) uses. Explore is pinned to that edition.

steps.label: You type the command
steps.what_ir0_does: ash forks cat. The path is /proc/version — a pseudo-file, not MINIX.
steps.why_it_matters: Same open/read/write as any file. The backend is procfs.

steps.label: VFS lookup
steps.what_ir0_does: Path walk hits the /proc mount. No disk inode for this file.
steps.why_it_matters: Pseudo-fs and on-disk FS share the open/read contract.

steps.label: proc_version_read
steps.what_ir0_does: Builds one line: IR0 version, utsname, build date/time, user@host, compiler.
steps.why_it_matters: Not a placeholder. ktest proc_version_contract opens this path.

steps.label: The line hits the TTY
steps.what_ir0_does: cat writes the buffer to fd 1. You read the edition the kernel was built as.
steps.why_it_matters: Guide edition and /proc/version should tell the same story.
